Sequential AIPE Check for the Standardized Mean

Source: R/seq_aipe_sm.R
seq_aipe_sm.Rd

Checks, with the data collected so far, whether enough observations are in hand for a confidence interval for the population standardized mean \(\mu/\sigma\) (the mean in standard deviation units; for difference scores, the standardized mean change) that is no wider than a chosen width, without assuming normality and without a planning value. The standardized mean is one of the effect sizes covered by the sequential accuracy in parameter estimation (AIPE) procedure of Kelley, Darku, and Chattopadhyay (2018, Example 3).

Usage

seq_aipe_sm(x, width, conf_level = 0.95)

Arguments

x

A numeric vector: the observations collected so far, at least 4 of them. Missing or infinite values are an error.

width

The target full width of the confidence interval for \(\mu/\sigma\) (\(\omega\) in the cited article): the upper limit minus the lower limit, in standard deviation units. A single positive number.

conf_level

The confidence level of the interval, a single number strictly between 0 and 1. Default 0.95.

Value

An object of class c("smsd_check", "data.frame") (see smsd_check_methods for its print(), summary(), and tidy() methods) with one row per quantity and columns term and value. The rows are, in order:

lower_limit

the lower confidence limit (NA when the variance estimate is not yet usable or the estimate cannot be computed; see the section below);

sm

the estimated standardized mean (NA when the sample has no variation);

upper_limit

the upper confidence limit (NA whenever lower_limit is);

xi_squared

the estimated asymptotic variance \(\hat{\xi}_n^2\), at least \(n^{-3}\) (the bound itself when the estimate is not yet usable);

criterion_n

the sample size the stopping rule currently requires (at least current_n + 1 when the variance estimate is not yet usable or the estimate cannot be computed);

current_n

the current sample size.

The object also carries these attributes:

is_satisfied

TRUE when the stopping rule is met, otherwise FALSE; never NA, and always identical to current_n >= criterion_n;

method

the string "standardized mean";

current_n, criterion_n

the values in the rows of those names;

conf_level, width

the values supplied;

variance_unusable

TRUE when the raw variance estimate is zero, negative, or not finite (see the section below), otherwise FALSE;

notes

a character vector, empty unless something needs explaining.

Details

The function evaluates the stopping rule once and returns. The user collects the pilot sample (see seq_aipe_sm_pilot), calls seq_aipe_sm(), and, while the rule is not met, adds one or more observations and calls it again. The function prints nothing and keeps no state.

Estimate. The standardized mean is estimated by \(\bar{X}_n / s_n\). Any real mean is allowed (the estimate is negative when the sample mean is); only a sample with no variation at all cannot be used.

Stopping rule. Sampling stops at the first \(n\), at or after the pilot size, with $$n \ge \left\lceil \frac{4 z_{\alpha/2}^2}{\omega^2} \left(\hat{\xi}_n^2 + \frac{1}{n}\right) \right\rceil$$ (their Equation 22), and the reported interval is \(\bar{X}_n / s_n \pm z_{\alpha/2} \hat{\xi}_n / \sqrt{n}\) (their Equation 23). Whenever the rule is met, the width of that interval is at most width. The article names the standardized mean as a member of its class of effect sizes but does not print its asymptotic variance. It follows from the article's Theorem 1 by the delta method: $$\xi^2 = 1 - \frac{\mu \mu_3}{\sigma^4} + \frac{\mu^2 (\mu_4 - \sigma^4)}{4 \sigma^6},$$ where \(\mu_3\) and \(\mu_4\) are the third and fourth central moments (for normal data this is \(1 + (\mu/\sigma)^2/2\)). The estimate \(\hat{\xi}_n^2\) substitutes the sample mean and variance and the unbiased central moment estimators of the article's Equations 78 and 79.

What the guarantee is. The width guarantee is exact. The coverage guarantee is asymptotic: coverage approaches conf_level as width shrinks (their Theorem 2). In simulated studies with a 95% interval and one observation added at each stage, coverage for normal data with \(\mu/\sigma = 0.4\) was 0.949 at width = 0.4 (6,000 studies, about 105 observations at the end) and 0.956 at width = 0.2 (2,000 studies, about 415 observations). For right skewed data (a standardized chi square distribution with 3 degrees of freedom, shifted so that \(\mu/\sigma = 1\)) it was 0.893 at width = 0.4 and 0.940 at width = 0.2: with skewed data the variance estimate runs low in small samples, so the procedure stops early on average (at 62 observations where the known variance would require 84, and at 289 where it would require 334). The variance estimate was zero or negative in fewer than 1% of the pilot samples, and positive but below \(n^{-3}\), so that the bound was used and the rule met with an interval far narrower than requested, in 2 of the 6,000 studies with skewed data at width = 0.4 and in no other. Use seq_aipe_sm_sensitivity to study a planned study before collecting data.

Estimates That Are Not Yet Usable

When the raw variance estimate is zero (exactly, or to within rounding error), negative, or not finite, which is common at small sample sizes for some effect sizes, or when the point estimate cannot be computed (a sample with no variation, where values that agree to ten significant digits count as equal), the check reports the stopping rule as not met, sets attr(out, "variance_unusable") to TRUE, and attaches a note that print() shows; see smsd_check_methods. This is a deliberate departure from the stopping rule as printed in the source articles, under which the lower bound \(n^{-3}\) would stand in for such an estimate and the rule would be met at once with an interval far narrower than requested; a positive estimate, however small, is used as the articles prescribe (the larger of it and \(n^{-3}\)).

References

Kelley, K., Darku, F. B., & Chattopadhyay, B. (2018). Accuracy in parameter estimation for a general class of effect sizes: A sequential approach. Psychological Methods, 23(2), 226–243. doi:10.1037/met0000127

Maxwell, S. E., Kelley, K., & Rausch, J. R. (2008). Sample size planning for statistical power and accuracy in parameter estimation. Annual Review of Psychology, 59, 537–563. doi:10.1146/annurev.psych.59.103006.093735

See also

seq_aipe_sm_pilot for the pilot size and seq_aipe_sm_sensitivity to simulate the procedure before collecting data. In DMAR: ss_aipe_sm, the fixed sample size analog for when a planning value is available, and ci_sm.

Other seq_aipe_sm: seq_aipe_sensitivity, seq_aipe_sm_pilot()

Author

Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu, Francis Bilson Darku fbilsond@nd.edu, Bhargab Chattopadhyay bhargab@iiitvadodara.ac.in

Examples

# By how many standard deviations does a reading score change from fall
# to spring? The data are the students' change scores, and the aim is a
# 95% confidence interval for the standardized mean change that is no
# wider than 0.50.
set.seed(113)
m <- seq_aipe_sm_pilot(width = 0.50)
change <- rnorm(m, mean = 4, sd = 10)
out <- seq_aipe_sm(change, width = 0.50)
out
#> Sequential check (standardized mean)
#> 
#>   Current n       : 8
#>   Criterion n     : 69
#>   Target width    : 0.5
#>   Confidence level: 95%
#>   Coverage        : asymptotic; assess with sensitivity analysis
#> 
#>   lower_limit       : -0.6051389
#>   sm                : 0.0815806
#>   upper_limit       : 0.7683001
#>   xi_squared        : 0.9820929
#>   criterion_n       : 69
#>   current_n         : 8
#> 
#>   Stopping rule met: FALSE

# The rule is not met at the pilot. Add one student at a time and check
# again, until it is.
while (!attr(out, "is_satisfied")) {
  change <- c(change, rnorm(1, mean = 4, sd = 10))
  out <- seq_aipe_sm(change, width = 0.50)
}
out
#> Sequential check (standardized mean)
#> 
#>   Current n       : 75
#>   Criterion n     : 75
#>   Target width    : 0.5
#>   Confidence level: 95%
#>   Coverage        : asymptotic; assess with sensitivity analysis
#> 
#>   lower_limit       : 0.200412
#>   sm                : 0.4477031
#>   upper_limit       : 0.6949941
#>   xi_squared        : 1.193938
#>   criterion_n       : 75
#>   current_n         : 75
#> 
#>   Stopping rule met: TRUE
